A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GlobalHealthAtlas, Public-Evaluator and Public-Model, with directly matchable methods and experiments. All pages are readable. v1 ends after its references despite unresolved appendix references; v2 supplies Appendices A-I.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluator validation, multilingual benchmarking, fine-tuning ablations, data-scaling experiments, cross-domain transfer and input-perturbation results in Tables 3-9.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds clinical-model comparisons, human dataset assessment, evaluator validation, weighting sensitivity tests and checkpoint-interpolation results.

M1.justification: Section 3.2.2 replaces v1's universal quality weights with format-specific weights: single-choice retains 0.45/0.25/0.20/0.10, while QA uses 0.25/0.35/0.25/0.15. Section 4.5 also introduces base/SFT checkpoint interpolation. These are limited procedural revisions; the core construction pipeline, six-dimensional evaluator and LoRA approach remain.

E1.justification: The corpus retains 280,210 instances, 15 domains, 17 languages and the same question formats. Public-health, clinical and general-science benchmark coverage is retained. The new clinical-gap and evaluator checks reuse already represented clinical/public-health data; appendix heatmaps disclose existing coverage. Additional datasets in Table 1 are related-work comparisons, not newly evaluated benchmarks.

E2.justification: v2 adds Medical_Model, AntAngelMed and BAICHUAN-M3 to a clinical/public-health comparison and a GPT-5 general-medical evaluator to the MedQA validation. DeepSeek-R1 and Kimi-k2-thinking are newly included specifically in evaluator Table 3. Table 7 additionally evaluates Qwen3.5-122B-A10B before and after SFT, substantially broadening the comparisons.

E3.justification: Added protocols include a 5:1 clinical training/test split for Medical_Model, assessment of 14,010 dataset items by 14 experts, and comparison of evaluators on 100 GPT-5 MedQA responses. Appendix B introduces 100-sample weighting experiments using Kendall's tau and top-10% overlap. These are additional designs; the original held-out benchmark and SFT evaluation sample sizes remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds human verification of dataset quality, sensitivity to perturbed versus uniform quality weights, an out-of-domain evaluator check, and interpolation analysis addressing the specialization/transfer tradeoff. Appendix H supplies three tobacco-domain failure cases and their scored responses. These substantially expand the diagnostic evidence beyond v1's retained scaling, SFT and perturbation analyses.

E5.justification: Tables 16 and 18 newly disclose training seed 42 for the evaluator and Public-Model. Appendix E specifies the agreement estimators and repeated-run calculations. The existing ten-run stability assessment is retained; neither an increased run count nor new confidence-interval reporting is established.

E6.justification: The main benchmark table is unchanged between v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 5. Substantial new results include the human quality score of 4.503/5, clinical and evaluator comparisons, weighting sensitivity, Qwen3.5 SFT results and full domain/language breakdowns. Table 10 newly reports interpolation scores of 6.512 on GlobalHealthAtlas and 7.545 on MMLU-pro. Table 7 also corrects the Qwen3-8B publichealth-qa decrement from 0.299 to 0.423.

T1.justification: v1 asserts theoretical guarantees but supplies no referenced proofs. v2 Appendix G adds a formal quality/noise assumption, a score-filtration risk theorem and proof, and Gaussian conditional-variance and arbitration derivations. This is substantial new formal content, separate from the added explanations of standard evaluation metrics.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the multilingual public-health corpus and construction pipeline, the six-dimensional Public-Evaluator, and domain adaptation through Public-Model. The new clinical-gap experiments support the existing argument for specialized public-health evaluation. The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same substantive research claims.

C2.justification: Appendix H adds substantive interpretations involving precision hallucination, demographic constraints being overridden by general priors, and plausible explanations masking factual errors. Appendix D.4 adds arguments about stylistic bias and the evaluator's size/stability tradeoff. The Impact Statement expands limitations to source harmonization and funding-related publication bias, beyond the retained geographic and linguistic caveats.

D1.justification: Appendices B-F supply previously missing generation and scoring prompts, detailed rubrics, response-source composition, arbitration instructions, inference hardware and settings, and LoRA/training configurations. The abstract adds code, evaluator and model release links. These substantially improve documented reproducibility, predominantly through disclosure rather than demonstrated reruns of retained experiments.

R1.justification: Table 1 expands the resource comparison with HealthSearchQA, ApolloCorpora, MMedC and AfriMed-QA, with corresponding citations. Other citations are added, including Mega-RAG, while the related-work organization and central research gap remain largely unchanged. Numerous publication and bibliographic updates refer to already cited works.

P1.justification: v2 adds an extensive explanatory structure in Appendices A-I, including complete procedural descriptions, scoring rubrics and supporting discussions where v1 had unresolved references. It also retitles the paper, revises the abstract and Impact Statement, expands author/affiliation information and repairs cross-references. The main section sequence remains largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the displays with clinical and evaluator comparison tables, sensitivity and configuration tables, dataset examples, distribution heatmaps and multilingual radar plots. The construction pipeline is redrawn and moved to Appendix B, and evaluator workflow displays are added. Existing benchmark tables and the scaling plot are largely retained and renumbered; dataset statistics move into Figure 1's caption.

improvement.justification: v1's reproducibility and reliability claims lacked the promised prompts, configurations and supporting appendices. v2 supplies these materials and adds a large human quality audit, weighting sensitivity tests and direct evaluator checks, substantially improving auditability and empirical support. Some inconsistencies remain, notably between Algorithm 1 and the appendix arbitration rules, while the theoretical guarantees depend on strong assumptions and approximations. These limitations temper the claims but do not outweigh the substantial documentation and validation gains.
